bullets.title: AMD: Citi raises PT to $800, Mizuho to $705 on Meta Muse / agentic AI CPU TAM explosion
bullets.body: Citi's Atif Malik raises AMD PT to $800 (from prior) as the primary CPU beneficiary of Meta Muse, projecting the CPU TAM to expand from $29B (2025) to $300B (2030) at a ~60% CAGR driven by always-on agentic AI vs. idle chatbots. AMD CEO Lisa Su confirmed plans to 'substantially increase' supply in 2027, citing 'very high' demand for several years. Mizuho separately raised AMD PT to $705 from $580 (Outperform); JPM channel checks echo multi-year AMD share-gain thesis with AMD-based architectures already in 2027 proposals.

bullets.title: META: Citi raises to Buy, $800 PT; Muse projects $27B+ revenue at scale on 6.6M downloads
bullets.body: Citi upgrades META to Buy with an $800 PT, projecting Muse could generate $8B in Year 1 revenue at a 5% take rate on ~$170B transaction volume, scaling to $23B+ in a Blue Sky scenario as Muse reshapes ~$16.5T of transaction value across 11 verticals. Muse has 6.6M+ downloads, 1.8M DAUs, and held the #1 most-downloaded app rank for 16 consecutive days. Separately, META reduced internal Claude Code users from 60K to 30K (spending >$105M in a 28-day period) and is building proprietary AI coding tools targeting $5-10B in 3P model cost savings.

bullets.title: NVDA: Reaffirmed Buy ($315 PT) at Citi; nearing $6T market cap on GPU demand from Muse agents
bullets.body: Citi reiterates NVDA Buy at $315 PT, noting Muse at 100M DAUs would require 200K-390K Blackwell-class GPUs worth $7-19B in one-time revenue, with each incremental million agentic DAUs worth $70-190M to NVDA. GS notes NVDA is up 5 of 6 sessions since the $150B buyback announcement and is approaching a $6T market cap. MS sees NVDA relatively insulated from AI power constraints.

bullets.title: MRVL: Investor Day today; Piper targets $45B FY31 revenue / $19 EPS; UBS raises PT to $335
bullets.body: MRVL Investor Day is today with management expected to introduce a new LT financial model potentially stretching to FY31 ($45B revenue, ~$19 EPS, ~45% CAGR). Piper flags the 'XPU Attach' opportunity as underestimated, using Google's $120B TPU deal as a proxy. UBS raises PT to $335 (from $310), modeling $20B revenue / $7.50 EPS in FY28 and $30B / $12 EPS in FY29, but cautions on crowded positioning and a potential sell-the-news reaction. OPCO echoes the $12B+ CY28 AI revenue target and flags ANET, CRDO, LITE, COHR as key adjacencies.

bullets.title: SHOP: JPM raises PT to $200, reiterates top pick; agentic commerce + 30% 2027E revenue growth path
bullets.body: JPM raises SHOP December 2027 PT from $185 to $200 (based on ~23x 2028E gross profit), reiterating OW and Analyst Focus List status. SHOP has delivered five consecutive quarters of 30%+ GMV and revenue growth; 2027 revenue modeled at +27% FXN with FCF margin of 19.6%. Shop Pay is integrated into Meta Muse and OpenAI ChatGPT, converting AI purchases at ~2x the rate of traditional channels, and has overtaken PayPal Venmo as the lowest-churn checkout button.

bullets.title: GOOGL + CEG: 890 MW / $4.3B nuclear deal confirmed; CEG +8.4% pre-market
bullets.body: Google and Constellation Energy confirmed a 20-year PPA for 890 MW of new nuclear capacity on the PJM grid, representing more than $4.3B of new investment by CEG with first uprate expected by 2028, plus an additional 15-year supply agreement for 2,700 MW across 11 Constellation nuclear units. CEG was up ~8.4% pre-market on the news. Separately, Roth notes CEG trades higher while GOOGL's X division is reducing moonshot development costs 10-20% annually via AI.

bullets.title: HUBS: 7% RIF, $65-75M charges; reaffirms all FY26 guidance; raises FY30 op margin target to 30%
bullets.body: HubSpot announced a restructuring eliminating ~7% of its workforce effective October 1, with $65-75M in charges (mostly severance, majority in Q4 FY26). The company reaffirms Q3 EPS guidance of $3.25-3.27 ex-items (consensus $3.27) and FY26 revenue guidance of $3.678-3.686B (consensus $3.68B). The FY30 non-GAAP operating margin target was raised to 30% from a prior 25%, with FY26-27 targets reaffirmed at 21% and 23-24%.

bullets.title: MU: Settles Netlist patent dispute for $600M; memory supply tightening through FY28
bullets.body: Micron and Netlist entered a patent license and settlement agreement covering server DIMMs and HBM technologies; Micron will pay $30M/quarter from Q4 2026 through Q3 2031 ($600M total), resolving all ITC and district court actions. UBS separately notes Micron sees tighter memory supply through FY28 with bit growth constrained to low-20%s (DRAM) / mid-20%s (NAND), and Micron raised FY27 capex guidance to $50B+. DRAM lead times are now at 20 weeks with worsening squeeze expected through 2027.

bullets.title: STX: Down pre-market; competing with Toshiba for TDK's HDD magnetic-heads business
bullets.body: Seagate and Toshiba are competing to acquire TDK's HDD magnetic heads business, with a deal potentially worth several billion dollars. Toshiba initiated talks in spring 2026; Seagate made a higher offer in summer. The competitive dynamic is pressuring STX pre-market. HDD lead times are now at 50 weeks per MS, with the memory/HDD squeeze worsening through 2027.

bullets.title: TSM: FY26 guidance raised to low-to-mid 40% growth; 2027 capex modeled $75-85B; Texas second fab cluster under consideration
bullets.body: TSMC expects to raise FY26 revenue growth guidance from +40% to low-to-mid 40s, with 4Q guiding up 10-15% q/q. GS SEMS raises TSMC's 2027E capex to $85B (from $78B) and 2028E to $98B (from $82B). TSMC is reportedly evaluating a second US fab cluster in Texas with up to six advanced wafer fabs; total Texas investment could exceed the $265B Arizona commitment. TSMC is also in discussions with Tesla/SpaceX for US semiconductor capacity.

bullets.title: HUT: MS site tour confirms River Bend multi-GW expansion on track; AI conversion demand rising
bullets.body: Morgan Stanley's site tour of HUT's River Bend Louisiana campus found ~1,100 workers daily, Phase 1 substation at 330 MW, and Data Hall 1 power expected within 'a couple months.' The $180M Poolin acquisition adds 230 MW, bringing active electrons for mining to 900 MW. Management targets multi-GW capacity with 'no identified gating items,' and noted existing customers are touring HUT sites for AI conversion opportunities.

bullets.title: BE: MS ranks Bloom Energy #1 in behind-the-meter power; $240B TAM through 2029
bullets.body: Morgan Stanley's distributed power framework forecasts ~120 GW / $240B TAM for behind-the-meter solutions through 2029 (77 GW data center + 40 GW C&I), driven by the AI buildout colliding with grid power constraints. Bloom Energy's SOFC ranks #1 on MS's composite BTM scorecard; BorgWarner turbine generator ranks #2 with ~$1.2B EBITDA expected by 2030 (~35% of group total). Time-to-power is identified as equally important as cost-of-power for data center economics.

bullets.title: PINS: CFO hire (Amazon's James Dibbo) seen as modest positive; new CFO effective Oct 26
bullets.body: Pinterest appointed James Dibbo as CFO effective October 26, 2026; Dibbo joins from Amazon where he led finance for Amazon Ads, Prime Video, and MGM Studios. The quick hire process is seen as minimizing disruption; analysts view the appointment as a modest positive given his ads-monetization background directly applicable to PINS's growth strategy.

bullets.title: ANET + AI networking: Highest investor conviction in semis; DC switch market +52% Y/Y to $48B
bullets.body: JPM's hardware & networking model revision shows the DC Ethernet Switch market growing +52% Y/Y to $48B in 2026 with a +36% CAGR through 2030; ANET holds 20% share. The AI DC Switch segment grew +132% Y/Y to $26B in 2026 at a +42% CAGR. OPCO and Jefferies both flag ANET alongside CRDO, LITE, and COHR as the highest-conviction names in the AI infrastructure trade beyond GPUs.

bullets.title: MTSI: Jefferies bull case targets $15 EPS in CY28 vs Street $11; PDs + LEO + 1.6T ramp as drivers
bullets.body: Jefferies sees a bull case for MTSI at $15 CY28 EPS vs the Street's $11, driven by data center growth from photodetectors (PDs, $14 content/transceiver) and the 1.6T ramp, CW lasers, NPO contribution, and LEO satellite liftoff expected in 2H26. Silicon photonics demand is accelerating with 1.6T arriving earlier than expected and additive to 800G deployments.

bullets.title: BABA: Jefferies reaffirms bullish 2027 outlook; external cloud 50%+ YoY, $100B by FY31
bullets.body: Jefferies reaffirms its bullish 2027 China internet outlook for BABA, projecting external cloud revenue to grow 50%+ YoY in the Sep quarter with further acceleration in Dec-Q and Mar-Q, reaching $100B by FY31 and $160B by FY33 (40-45% CAGR). T-Head cumulative shipments reached 560K by April 2026 with V900/J900 releases planned for 1Q27/3Q28; T-Head's share of BABA compute expected to rise from 10% to 40-50%. MaaS revenue hit RMB20B by August vs. original RMB30B FY27 guidance.

bullets.title: APP: Sued by San Diego County over explicit ads shown to children's devices
bullets.body: San Diego County filed suit against AppLovin alleging the company bypassed parental controls to collect children's location data and serve adult-targeted ads in games played by minors. The litigation adds regulatory/legal risk to APP; multiple sources flagged this as a notable pre-market negative.

bullets.title: CRM + ADBE: Citi software bus tour signals mixed signals; CRM reacceleration expected in 2H
bullets.body: Citi's software bus tour found CRM management attempting to clarify ratable vs. license growth dynamics and Slack momentum, with 2H organic reacceleration expected. ADBE's freemium/MAU-first pivot is strategically sensible but ARR durability remains uncertain amid a leadership transition. ADSK and ZM were most constructive on AI opportunity among the group.

bullets.title: HOOD: EPS estimates raised +3% on higher volumes; preferred broker pick over SCHW
bullets.body: Jefferies raises HOOD and SCHW 2027 EPS estimates by an average of +3% on higher volumes, with broker/wealth fundamentals remaining solid on healthy NNA trends and stable client cash. HOOD is flagged as the preferred name in brokers/wealth alongside SCHW with improving earnings momentum.

bullets.title: ACN: Mizuho raises PT to $241 on AI enterprise adoption; F4Q26 revenue +7% YoY, bookings re-accelerate
bullets.body: Mizuho raises ACN PT to $241 from $226 (Outperform) following F4Q26 results showing revenue growth of +7% YoY well above guidance, with new bookings re-accelerating to +5% CC YoY. ACN's FY27 guidance of +3% to +6% CC revenue growth came in modestly above expectations. The enterprise AI adoption gap is expected to narrow as token costs decline, reinforcing the 'AI reinvention' thesis for ACN.
